question: For representative Stripe payment methods, what do official docs state about refund timing/failure, delayed failure notification, mandate authorization, finality, and capture/cancellation as of 2026-09-22?

scope.geography_or_context: Stripe payment methods documented on docs.stripe.com; method-specific scope, not API execution
exclusions: Stripe API calls, keys, test objects, non-official sources, undocumented typical behavior

claims.claim: ACH Direct Debit is a reusable delayed-notification method and acknowledgement of success or failure can take up to 4 business days.

sources.support: Method description states delayed notification and up to 4 business days.

claims.claim: ACH refunds may be submitted up to 180 days after original payment, are asynchronous and take up to 3 business days, and cannot be canceled.

sources.support: Refund section states submission window, processing time and cannot be canceled.

claims.claim: ACH refund final status is communicated by refund.updated or refund.failed; failure changes status to failed and returns amount to Stripe balance.

sources.support: Refund tracking section states webhook events and failure balance treatment.

claims.claim: ACH requires customer debit authorization/mandate and cancellation invalidates future debit requests.
ACH Direct Debit disputes are final and have no appeal process.

sources.support: Dispute section explicitly says final and no appeal.

claims.caveat: This is dispute finality, not a claim that every successful payment is absolutely irreversible.

claims.claim: SEPA Direct Debit refunds typically take 3-4 business days to process and funds arrive within 5 business days; submission is within 180 days.

sources.support: SEPA refund section states both windows and timing.

claims.claim: SEPA is reusable and delayed-notification; most failures occur within 6 business days and a 5-business-day refusal window follows submission.
claims.caveat: Rare failures can appear later as disputes.

claims.claim: SEPA requires a mandate and cancellation invalidates future debit requests; Stripe learns of cancellation after a failed attempt and sends mandate.updated.
SEPA Direct Debit disputes are final and cannot be appealed; Manual capture support is No.

sources.support: Dispute finality text and payment properties table.

claims.caveat: Finality refers to disputes; no general payment irreversibility claim is made.

claims.claim: Bacs confirmation takes 4 business days with an existing mandate and up to 7 business days with a new mandate.
Bacs may be reported as failed by the bank after Stripe marks it successful, in which case it is identified as a dispute.
Bacs refunds must be submitted within 180 days and typically take 3-4 business days; pending refund is canceled if the original Charge fails.

sources.support: Bacs refund timing and processing-state refund text.

claims.caveat: The page does not state a separate refund failure webhook.

claims.claim: Bacs requires a Direct Debit Instruction/mandate and cancellation invalidates future debit requests.
Bacs disputes can be submitted indefinitely and are final/non-appealable; Bacs retries can run up to twice within 30 days when enabled.
iDEAL | Wero gives immediate payment success/failure notification after bank authentication.
claims.caveat: Exact customer experience depends on the bank.

claims.claim: iDEAL refunds may be submitted up to 180 days; they may remain pending up to 7 days and are considered successful after 7 days without a failure signal.
claims.caveat: The page does not specify post-failure balance or webhook semantics.

claims.claim: iDEAL does not support manual capture.

sources.support: Payment properties table says Manual capture support No.

claims.claim: Konbini refunds require customer return-account information collected by Stripe through the confirmation email flow; completion timing is not stated.
claims.caveat: Refund failure and arrival time are not stated.

claims.claim: Konbini payment flow states the customer receives a notification that payment is complete after cash payment; Manual capture support is No.
Klarna refunds may be submitted up to 180 days, usually take 5-7 business days, cancel remaining payments and return already-paid amounts.
claims.caveat: May take longer depending on financial institution and purchase type.

claims.claim: Klarna supports full and partial refunds but not refunding a payment escalated to a dispute; Manual capture support is Yes.

sources.support: Klarna refund and payment properties sections.

claims.claim: For Klarna authorization scenarios where a down payment is collected, the general authorization page says it is refunded if not captured and the balance must be captured within 30 days.

sources.support: Klarna-specific row in authorization validity guidance.

claims.caveat: The page does not establish that this conditional rule applies to every Klarna configuration.

claims.claim: For ACH and Bacs, the official payment pages do not provide a directly stated method-specific automatic-cancellation rule when capture is not performed.

sources.support: Reviewed capabilities/refund sections; no such direct statement located.
Reviewed capabilities/refund sections; no such direct statement located.

claims.caveat: Requested semantic status: unknown (manifest validator accepts unverified as the corresponding no-direct-evidence status). Unknown is retained rather than inferred from generic card authorization behavior.

claims.claim: The reviewed official pages do not state general payment irreversibility/finality for iDEAL, Konbini, or Klarna.
claims.caveat: Requested semantic status: unknown (manifest validator accepts unverified as the corresponding no-direct-evidence status). This does not contradict method-specific dispute-support table values.

claims.claim: The reviewed official pages do not state general refund-failure notification and balance treatment for SEPA, Bacs, iDEAL, Konbini, or Klarna beyond the method-specific statements recorded above.

sources.support: No direct general refund-failure semantics found.
Only pending-refund cancellation on Charge failure is stated.

claims.caveat: Requested semantic status: unknown (manifest validator accepts unverified as the corresponding no-direct-evidence status). Unknown means not explicitly stated in reviewed official pages.
